title: PANTOZOL Control 20 mg gastro-resistant tablets: summary of product characteristics (EPAR product information, Annex I)
authors: European Medicines Agency; marketing authorisation holder Takeda GmbH
journal: European Medicines Agency, European public assessment report, product information; EU/1/09/517; first authorised 12 June 2009, renewed 21 February 2014; PDF file dated May 2023
funder: not stated; regulatory product information carries no funding statement
result: Non-prescription pantoprazole 20 mg once daily for short-term treatment of reflux symptoms in adults; treatment should not exceed 4 weeks without consulting a doctor. Section 4.4: reduced acidity raises gastric bacterial counts and slightly increases the risk of Salmonella, Campylobacter and Clostridium difficile infection; severe cutaneous adverse reactions (erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, DRESS), which can be life-threatening or fatal, frequency not known; very infrequent subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, with risk of recurrence on another PPI; chromogranin A rise interferes with neuroendocrine tumour investigations. Risks of long-term use: reduced vitamin B12 absorption; hip, wrist and spine fracture, predominantly in the elderly, with observational studies suggesting a 10% to 40% increase in overall fracture risk, some of it possibly due to other risk factors; severe hypomagnesaemia reported rarely after at least 3 months and in most cases a year, with fatigue, tetany, delirium, convulsions, dizziness and ventricular arrhythmia, possibly leading to hypocalcaemia and hypokalaemia, in most patients improving after magnesium replacement and discontinuation. Section 4.8: fundic gland polyps (benign) common; agranulocytosis rare; tubulointerstitial nephritis with possible progression to renal failure, hepatocellular failure, microscopic colitis, hyponatraemia and hallucination frequency not known. Section 5.1: fasting gastrin doubles in most cases during long-term treatment, with a mild to moderate increase in ECL cells in a minority; carcinoid precursors or gastric carcinoids, as seen in animals, have not been observed in humans. Section 5.3: 2-year rat studies produced gastric neuroendocrine neoplasms, attributed to massively elevated serum gastrin; liver tumours in rats and female mice and thyroid neoplastic changes in rats at 200 mg/kg; reduced bone growth in rat offspring at exposures about twice human clinical exposure.
